tasks.brief: Fix the corrupt-primary load path in src/services/storage.py. The current build already: reads the persisted generation under the lock and passes it as expected_revision; accepts a top-level JSON list as the legacy primary shape at revision 0; never auto-falls-back to reading .bak. Do NOT retouch those already-landed branches. The one remaining correction: WHEN the primary file exists but json.load raises JSONDecodeError inside load_versioned_snapshot (the JSON-parse-failure branch — NOT the invalid-envelope branch and NOT the missing-file branch), SHALL quarantine it by rename to '<primary-name>.corrupt-<stamp>' in the same directory, preserving its bytes exactly, then return ([], 0). Use a time-based stamp (e.g. int(time.time())) or a monotonic counter. Quarantined files are never deleted, never overwritten by later saves, never auto-restored. Keep public surface: load_snapshot(), save_snapshot(), quarantine_files(), load_versioned_snapshot(), save_versioned_snapshot(), SnapshotConflict. The lock must be held when the rename happens so a concurrent save cannot race the quarantine. Acceptance: tests/test_storage_service.py::test_corrupt_snapshot_is_quarantined passes — after loading a primary whose bytes are not valid JSON, a '.corrupt-' entry exists beside the data file and the primary path no longer exists; and test_corrupt_file_loads_empty still passes — load returns ([], 0).

Extend src/api/threads.py for revisioned persistence per ERD-DELTA v73 prescription. Extend ThreadsPayload with required revision: int >= 0 (contracts schema ThreadsPayload.revision). Add a DELETE body model containing required revision: int >= 0 (contracts schema ThreadsRevisionPrecondition). GET performs one revisioned load (load_versioned_snapshot) and returns {"threads": [...], "revision": n, "quarantined": bool} — quarantined true iff quarantine_files() finds a .corrupt-* entry. PUT calls save_versioned_snapshot(payload.threads, payload.revision); DELETE calls save_versioned_snapshot([], body.revision). Both return {"status":"ok", "revision": n+1} (the returned new revision). Map SnapshotConflict to HTTP 409 with the exact top-level JSON body {"error":"revision_conflict", "current_revision": n} — do NOT wrap in FastAPI's detail; use a plain JSONResponse or set the body directly. Validation failures (missing/invalid revision) remain 422 and write nothing. Do not change the chat route or other handlers. Acceptance: all mapped API tests pass — test_get_with_no_saved_data_returns_empty, test_put_then_get_roundtrips, test_optional_fields_default, test_put_malformed_payload_is_422_and_preserves_stored, test_put_invalid_role_rejected, test_put_without_revision_is_422_and_writes_nothing, test_delete_without_revision_is_422_and_writes_nothing, test_each_accepted_put_advances_revision, test_each_accepted_delete_advances_revision, test_stale_put_leaves_primary_and_backup_unchanged, test_stale_delete_leaves_primary_and_backup_unchanged, test_two_concurrent_same_revision_puts_have_one_winner, test_delete_clears_snapshot, test_get_reports_quarantine_after_corrupt_snapshot, test_put_threads_roundtrips_sources.

Own the authoritative hydrated revision, ordered persist queue, and conflict latch in src/static/threads.js, per ERD-DELTA v73 prescription. Every persistence-worthy mutation (PUT of a complete snapshot and DELETE) captures its own complete snapshot at enqueue time. Run at most one PUT/DELETE at a time (serialize the queue). The first request uses the hydrated revision; after a 200, adopt the response revision before issuing the next queued snapshot. Do not coalesce or reorder mutations. Ordinary network/non-409 failures preserve AC-75/AC-76 ('not saved') and do NOT advance revision. On a 409: clear pending snapshots, latch the page against every later PUT/DELETE, and write exactly 'history changed elsewhere — reload required' to save-status. Only document reload clears the latch. Expose the minimum hook app.js needs to install the GET revision before a mutation can enqueue — e.g. window.Threads.setHydratedRevision(revision) (or a documented equivalent) called by app.js during startup hydration. Keep existing public surface (renderSidebar, switchThread, createThread, etc.) intact; do not restate carried behavior. Acceptance: the D-64 browser tests map to app.js, so T3's acceptance is the smoke_check plus the mapped backend tests passing; specifically threads.js must contain 'revision' and the exact latch string 'history changed elsewhere — reload required'.

During startup GET hydration in src/static/app.js, install BOTH data.threads and data.revision into the threads persistence owner (the hook T3 exposes) before rendering or creating state. A healthy reload starts with empty save-status and an unlatch. If GET is empty, default-thread creation is the first queued save against the returned revision (revision 0). Never infer a revision from content — always use the data.revision field. Do not restate carried app.js behavior (chat surface, SSE, pollStatus, etc.). Keep the existing init order: hydration happens before renderSidebar/current-chat refresh. Acceptance: the D-64 browser tests pass — test_browser_serializes_rapid_mutations_in_revision_order, test_browser_conflict_warns_and_stops_further_writes, test_reload_after_conflict_hydrates_and_allows_a_new_save — and the smoke_check 'revision' grep holds. This task is final and its dependency closure covers every implementation file (T1, T2, T3).
